records.name: Friends of Three Bears Park
records.summary: Neighbors who look after Three Bears Park on Delancey Street: they raise money through community events, keep the park clean and planted, and host seasonal gatherings such as an Easter egg hunt.
records.what_you_do: Help with the spring Love Your Park clean-up or a fall festival, or come out to Park after Dark and the Halloween event.

schedule.text: Clean-ups and park events through the year, including a spring Love Your Park clean-up, a fall festival, Park after Dark, a Halloween event and an Easter egg hunt. The page lists no exact dates.

cost.text: The page lists no fees for events or volunteering. The group pays for upkeep through its own annual fundraisers.

first_step.how: Email threebearspark@gmail.com to ask about the next clean-up or park event and how to join in.
first_step.basis: Events and clean-ups are public, but the page does not say how to sign up to volunteer.

records.notes: Batch name was Friends of Delancy Street Park. The group's own site calls it Friends of Three Bears Park, also known as Friends of Delancey Street Park, and gives 319 Delancey Street (the IRS list says 311). Site says incorporated in 1989. No dated items on the page; the copyright year is not counted as evidence, so status is probably_active on the working-site rule. Re-check next wave for dated events.

records.name: Friends of Eastern State Penitentiary Park
records.summary: Volunteers who care for the green spaces around Eastern State Penitentiary: they pick up trash, plant trees, run community events, and keep garden plots and playground areas in shape.
records.what_you_do: Join a trash pickup or tree planting day, help at a community event, or take on a garden plot.

schedule.text: Trash pickups, tree plantings and community events through the year. The site has a community events page and a volunteer page, but lists no dates.

locations.label: Corinthian Gardens, Brown Street Lawn and Playpen Playground

cost.text: Donations and sponsorships are invited. The page lists no fees for volunteering.

first_step.how: Use the Volunteer link on fespp.org, or email fespp19130@gmail.com to ask about the next trash pickup or planting day.
first_step.basis: The volunteer link and a listed email make the way in clear, and the group posts volunteer days.

records.notes: IRS legal name: Friends of Eastern State Penitentiary Inc. The site lists no dated events or news. Its newsletter sign-up page shows a note that storage is not set up yet, so the newsletter may not work. The PO box on the IRS list is for mail only; the physical address is on Brown Street.

records.name: Friends of Historic Sedgeley
records.summary: Supporters who help keep up the Sedgeley Club Boathouse and the Turtle Rock lighthouse on Boathouse Row. They invite volunteers and gifts, and they welcome visitors to the boathouse.
records.what_you_do: Sign up through the volunteer page, give or sponsor, or come visit the boathouse on Kelly Drive.

schedule.text: The site lists no dated events. It has pages for visiting the boathouse and for volunteering.

cost.text: The site invites gifts and sponsorships. No fees were listed.

first_step.how: Email info@friendsofhistoricsedgeley.org to ask how to start volunteering at the boathouse.
first_step.basis: The site has a volunteer page and a listed email, but the volunteer steps on that page were not read, so the way in is not confirmed.

records.notes: No dated items, so status rests on the working site alone. The only dates on the site are historical (1887, 1897, 1902). The Volunteer and Come Visit Us pages exist but were not read. The site has a contact form as well as the listed email.

records.notes: No website found. The batch website field held a name, not a web address. One search found a GuideStar profile with the same EIN and the same address as the IRS list. records.name: Friends of the Rail Park
records.summary: Volunteers and supporters developing the Rail Park, a three-mile greenway on old rail tracks from Northern Liberties to Fairmount Park. Phase One is already open, and the group runs clean-ups, green-ups and guided tours.
records.what_you_do: Join the October 14 volunteer clean-up or the October 21 green-up, or book a guided tour of the park.

schedule.text: October 2026 events: a park tour and a hip hop dance event on Saturday Oct 10, a volunteer clean-up on Wednesday Oct 14, a volunteer green-up on Wednesday Oct 21, and a Furry Friends tour on Saturday Oct 24. The park is open daily, 7 am to 10 pm.

cost.text: The park is free to visit. Donations are tax-deductible, and the site also offers membership.

first_step.how: Email friends@therailpark.org or call 215-485-2221 to ask how to join the October 14 clean-up or the October 21 green-up.
first_step.basis: Volunteer days and tours are posted publicly with a clear contact, and the park is free and open daily.

records.notes: Batch alias: Viaductgreene. IRS mailing address is PO Box 23, 19105. Membership is mentioned on the donate page, but its details were not shown. The Get Involved page was not read, so the exact sign-up steps are not confirmed.

records.name: Friends of the South Street Police Mini-Station
records.summary: Neighbors and local businesses that support the South Street police mini-station. They run toy, clothing and supply drives, bike rides and community nights, and raise money for station equipment.
records.what_you_do: Drop off a donation at 905 South Street, or come to a community night or a bike ride.

schedule.text: Events and drives come up a few times a year. Dated items include a community night in August 2024 and a safety workshop in October 2024. The site also lists monthly 3rd District police meetings. No upcoming dates are listed.

cost.text: Some events are free, such as the memorial bike ride. A 2024 safety workshop asked for an RSVP. Costs for other events are not listed.

first_step.how: Drop off a donation at 905 South Street, or sign up for the group's newsletter at policeministation.org.
first_step.basis: Events are public, but the page does not say how to volunteer or join the group.

records.notes: Newest explicit dated item is an October 2024 workshop, close to the 24 month edge. Later drives are dated by inference only, so they are not used. The email on the site belongs to the city station, not the group, so it is not recorded. Social handles on the site (Instagram friendsofsouthstministation, Twitter southstmini) were not confirmed as URLs. IRS mailing address is PO Box 63871.

records.name: Global Water Alliance
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that works on safe water, sanitation and hygiene around the world. It runs field projects and education programs, mentors young water professionals, and hosts talks and an annual conference.
records.what_you_do: Become a member, attend an event or the annual conference, or donate. The page does not list volunteer roles.

schedule.text: Events and the annual conference through the year. The site gives no dates for upcoming events.

cost.text: Membership and donations are offered. Prices were not shown on the page read.

first_step.how: Check the events page on globalwateralliance.net for the next talk, or become a member through the Become a Member page.
first_step.basis: Membership, events and a donation route are listed publicly, but volunteer roles are not described.

records.notes: No close vocabulary tag for global water work, so it is filed under talks and learning. Projects are described as rural and overseas, and the countries are not named. Its office is in Philadelphia. Contact page not read, so no email or phone is recorded. Other dated items are from 2025 (blog posts and a UN water meeting in July 2025).

records.name: Greater Philadelphia Law Library Association
records.summary: A regional group for law librarians and legal information workers in the Philadelphia area. It runs educational events and a spring institute, and it keeps a member directory, a job board and a members forum.
records.what_you_do: Join as a member to take part in events, the job board and the members forum. Students can apply for scholarships and grants.

schedule.text: Membership year runs June 1 to May 31. Events are on the group's upcoming events page, and newsletters go out each spring and winter.

cost.text: Annual membership dues. The amount was not shown on the pages read, and partial-year dues are not offered.

first_step.how: Join or renew through the Join us page at gplla.org, then check the upcoming events list.
first_step.basis: Dues come before you can see the events, and the site does not say whether non-members can attend.

records.notes: Regional chapter of the American Association of Law Libraries. The members forum sits behind a login, so nothing inside it was read. The email is the group's listed membership and webmaster contact. Event dates are on a separate page that was not read.

records.name: Greater Philadelphia Philosophy Consortium
records.summary: A consortium of philosophy programs and scholars across the Philadelphia area. It runs monthly discussion groups, free public talks and symposia, and an undergraduate conference.
records.what_you_do: Join a monthly discussion group, which meets on Zoom or in person, or come to a free public talk or symposium.

schedule.text: Discussion groups meet monthly in the evening, several of them on Zoom. Public talks and symposia come up a few times a term, and the blog lists dates for fall 2026.

cost.text: Most events are free and open to the public.

first_step.how: Pick a discussion group from the blog's discussion groups page and join its next meeting. The page lists the reading and the Zoom or room details.
first_step.basis: Most events are free and open to the public, and each discussion group posts its reading in advance.

records.notes: The IRS list address (808 S 7th St) does not appear on the site, and event venues are university rooms, so no location is recorded. The site's Contact page was not read. Discussion group contacts are on the discussion groups page and are not recorded here.

records.name: Hannah Callowhill Stage
records.notes: The website redirects to a blog for a podcast about an archaeology dig at 103 Callowhill St. No classes, membership, volunteer roles, shows or community programs are listed, so it is not a joinable group. Blog posts stop in November 2022.
